en: The Questions of Milinda;
The Questions of the Puzzles;
The Chapter on the Indivisible.
8. The Question on the Indivisible Assembly “Venerable Nāgasena, you say:
‘The Tathāgata has an indivisible assembly,’ and yet again you say:”
‘By Devadatta, in a single stroke, five hundred bhikkhus were split.
If, venerable Nāgasena, the Tathāgata has an indestructible assembly, then that statement that ‘by Devadatta, in a single stroke, five hundred bhikkhus were split’ is false.
If, by Devadatta, in a single stroke, five hundred bhikkhus were split, then the statement that ‘the Tathāgata has an indestructible assembly’ is also false.”
“This too is a double-edged question that has come to you;

it is profound, difficult to unravel, more knotty than a knot, and herein this people is obstructed, hindered, hemmed in, shut off, and enveloped. Herein, display your power of wisdom against the doctrines of others.

“Great King, the Tathāgata is one whose assembly is indivisible. Although Devadatta caused five hundred bhikkhus to be split asunder by a single stroke, that was through the power of the schismatic. Great King, when a schismatic exists, there is nothing called ‘indivisible.’”
When there is a cause for division, even a mother is divided from her son, and a son is divided from his mother;
a father is divided from his son, and a son is divided from his father; a brother is divided from his sister, and a sister is divided from her brother;
even a companion is divided from his companion; and even a boat, though constructed from a combination of various woods, is broken apart by the impact of the force of the waves.
Even a tree, though endowed with sweet-tasting fruit, breaks when struck by the forceful power of the wind; even gold of noble origin is broken by iron.
Moreover, Great King, it is not the intention of the wise, nor the conviction of the Buddhas, nor the desire of the learned, that "the Tathāgata has a breakable assembly.
Yet there is a reason here why the Tathāgata is said to have an "unbreakable assembly."

What is the reason for this here, Great King? It has never been heard before that the assembly of the Tathāgata was ever split, even while he was wandering about from place to place, on account of any gift withheld, any unpleasant speech, any harmful conduct, or any lack of impartiality; that is the reason.
“The Tathāgata is called ‘one whose assembly is indivisible.

Therefore, Great King, you should know this: is there anything found in the ninefold word of the Buddha, recorded in the Suttas, according to which the assembly of the Tathāgata was split by something done by a Bodhisatta?
“There is nothing such, Bhante, nor is it seen or even heard of in the world.”
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! It is so; thus do I accept it.
This is the eighth dilemma concerning the indivisible assembly.
This is the second chapter on the indivisible.
In this chapter, there are eight questions.
